summary: This cycle is agents hitting the real world and bouncing. A 1036-point Maya-site writeup and a 681-point United Airlines booking ban sit next to Anthropic's IPO (1003 points, 917 comments) and Claude Fable 5.2 (923 points, 1054 comments). Google shipped Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Carbon, and a Decisions API in the same window Amazon claimed millions saved by swapping Sonnet for a specialized decider. Builder sentiment split in public: Jane Street's Socratic Tutor skill and Fable one-shot games on one side, unread AI codebases and 'is Opus nerfed' on the other. Skills became both the unit of work and the unit of risk (SkillSpector, SkillEvaluator). Reddit was blocked this run, so community signal is HN plus GitHub.

highlights.title: My AI agents found an unmapped Maya site?
highlights.why: The week's highest-point story is a field-research agent loop (maps, imagery, literature), not a model card. Treat the discovery claim with HN's skepticism, and treat the workflow as a bar for multi-tool agents that leave the IDE.

highlights.title: Anthropic IPO
highlights.why: Claude is now a public-market story. Builders on Anthropic APIs and Claude Code should treat vendor concentration, pricing, and terms as design constraints, not background noise.

highlights.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
highlights.why: The week's main Anthropic drop, and the largest comment thread. Coding-agent quality shifted enough that evals, prompts, and default-model choices need a re-run, not a patch. Mythos stays gated.

highlights.title: Is Opus 5.5 nerfed? Thinking patterns changed on November 3
highlights.why: Silent behavior change on a production coding model is an ops incident. Pin model IDs, log traces, and treat 'same name, different thinking' as a regression class you have to detect.

highlights.title: Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators
highlights.why: If your agent reads Gmail or Drive, user data may leave the model boundary. Privacy defaults and 'do not send PII to consumer Gemini' are product requirements, not footnotes.

highlights.title: Amazon saves millions by replacing Sonnet 4.6 with Strands Decider
highlights.why: Frontier models are being pulled out of high-volume agent routing in favor of cheaper specialized deciders. Put expensive LLMs behind a router and measure task-level ROI.

highlights.title: Socratic Tutor
highlights.why: Jane Street shipping a skill that teaches instead of dumping answers is a concrete SKILL.md pattern: constrain agent behavior with a small, opinionated prompt artifact. Repo: 8895 stars.

highlights.title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers
highlights.why: Incumbents are blocking unsupervised booking agents at the policy layer. Consumer-agent products need official APIs, identity, and human-in-the-loop checkout. Scraping as the user is becoming a banned path.

highlights.title: AlphaProof Code
highlights.why: DeepMind extending proof-search into code is a different coding-agent bet than chat-and-patch. Watch this if you care about verified generation, formal specs, and agents that search rather than sample.

highlights.title: AI usage generates a fragile codebase
highlights.why: The week's main 'coding agents rot the repo' thread. If you ship agent-written code, tests, ownership, and review gates belong in the agent loop, not as later cleanup.

highlights.title: All AI-generated code should be Open Source
highlights.why: Licensing and provenance of agent output is becoming a legal fight, not just a blog take. Assume customers will ask what training data and generation pipeline produced the code.

highlights.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
highlights.why: Google's fast execution model for everyday agent loops, paired in-thread with Antigravity Orchestrator switching Carbon and Hydrogen in-session. Re-benchmark tool use before locking a default.

tangentRadar.whyItMatters: The loudest non-model story is access. Airlines, search APIs, and consumer Gemini data paths are all drawing a line around unsupervised agents. Official APIs, identity, and human checkout are becoming the product, not scraping.

tangentRadar.topic: Harness and router over frontier weights
tangentRadar.whyItMatters: The largest cost claims this week are about routing and leaf models, not a new weights file. If a decider or a $0.10 worker moves the bill more than the planner, roadmaps that only track frontier releases are looking at the wrong layer.

tangentRadar.topic: Skills as work and as risk
tangentRadar.whyItMatters: SKILL.md is now a distribution format with a scanner and an eval harness. Frontmatter, model drift, and malicious skills are in the same conversation as 'how do I teach the agent'.

tangentRadar.topic: Fragile AI code vs one-shot demos
signals: AI usage generates a fragile codebase
All AI-generated code should be Open Source
tangentRadar.whyItMatters: The same week Fable one-shots a game, HN argues that AI code rot and licensing are the bill coming due. Speed is not the eval. Ownership, tests, and provenance are.
Labs are packaging planning plus tool execution as a product. Home-grown coordinators now compete with first-party workers, and the complaints are cost, fake tests, and review loops.
The GitHub and HF side of the feed is still local CLIs and open checkpoints. They do not always win HN, but they are what people run when APIs throttle or data cannot leave the box.

experimentQueue.title: Re-run the same repo task on Fable 5.2 vs Hydrogen vs last week's default
experimentQueue.why: Three labs shipped or GA'd coding models in one week. Keep the harness fixed so you learn about the model, not about prompt drift.
experimentQueue.prompt: Same AGENTS.md, same repo, same ticket. Fable 5.2 vs Gemini 4 Hydrogen vs last week's default. Compare diff quality, tokens, and whether a human can review the result.

experimentQueue.title: Put a cheap decider in front of the frontier planner
experimentQueue.why: Strands Decider and Gemini Decisions API are the same architectural bet: do not spend Sonnet on yes/no routing.
experimentQueue.prompt: Route classification, policy checks, and tool choice to a decider or Ember-class worker. Keep the planner on Fable or Carbon. Measure cost per merged PR.

experimentQueue.title: Scan your skill pack like it is supply chain
experimentQueue.why: SkillSpector and SkillEvaluator exist because skills are loadable code. A SKILL.md from the internet is an unreviewed dependency.
experimentQueue.prompt: Run SkillSpector on every skill your agents load. Add SkillEvaluator or a writtenFor field so a model bump does not silently change behavior.

experimentQueue.title: Audit one generated module for owners
experimentQueue.why: The fragile-codebase thread is the matching failure mode for this week's one-shot demos.
experimentQueue.prompt: Pick a module written mostly by agents in the last 90 days. Can two teammates explain it without the original session? If not, add tests and a human-owned map before the next agent pass.

method: Baseline generated by scripts/generate-agent-research.mjs (exit 0, 40 items). Generator ranked OpenAI customer stories and star-inflated GitHub repos above 1000-point HN threads.
HN Algolia search?tags=story_{id} for points and num_comments (not /items/{id} children). Window 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-16.

Official pages fetched: Anthropic Fable 5.2, Anthropic IPO, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Gemini Decisions API, Gemini 4 Carbon, AlphaProof Code, Muse Ember, Claude Sheets/Whiteboards, Claude Code Projects, OpenAI persistent-agents blog.
OpenAI consumer blog URLs (ChatGPT Wallet, Control Room, Businesses) returned 403 and were omitted.
GitHub metadata via gh api. Hugging Face public model API for likes/downloads. Reddit JSON returned 403; no Reddit items fabricated.
Ranking uses real HN points and verified star/like counts, not the generator score.
